buckets.title: Landing page components
buckets.description: Structural building blocks you rearrange to keep a single CTA honest.

terms.title: Hero
terms.shortDescription: The above-the-fold stage that introduces the offer and CTA immediately.
terms.definition: The hero pairs a clear headline, a proof-backed supporting line, and the primary CTA so visitors know what you do and what to do next without scrolling.
terms.whenToUse: Always—the hero is the first impression for any paid or organic visit.
aiPhrases: Draft a hero layout that locks headline, supporting copy, and CTA in a tight Z-pattern.
examples: Headline + subhead on the left, product mock and primary CTA on the right.

terms.title: Subhead
terms.shortDescription: One tight sentence that clarifies value right after the hero headline.
terms.definition: The subhead answers the immediate follow-up question the headline triggers—usually who it is for or what result they get next.
terms.whenToUse: Whenever the headline is bold or outcome-focused and needs context to feel believable.
aiPhrases: Write a subhead that names the audience and promises the outcome in under 18 words.
examples: Designed for growth teams shipping tests weekly

terms.title: Primary CTA
terms.shortDescription: The one action button styled for maximum contrast and clarity.
terms.definition: Your primary CTA uses an action verb, a benefit hint, and surrounding reassurance to make the click feel obvious.
terms.whenToUse: Always present in the hero and repeated within the flow where intent peaks.
aiPhrases: Give me three CTA variants that pair an active verb with the next-step benefit.
examples: Start the 7-day teardown

terms.title: Value props
terms.shortDescription: Three to five punchy proof-backed statements that ladder up to the promise.
terms.definition: Value props are scannable headlines with a short line of support that show how you deliver the main outcome.
terms.whenToUse: Use when visitors need to understand how the product/system works in their context.
aiPhrases: Summarize the top four outcomes as value props with proof metrics or specific details.
examples: Cut build time from weeks to hours with a subline about modular sections

terms.title: Features
terms.shortDescription: Deeper dives that show the mechanics behind each value prop.
terms.definition: Feature blocks combine visuals, captions, and specifics so buyers trust that the promised outcome is doable.
terms.whenToUse: After value props to let detail-oriented readers continue their evaluation.
aiPhrases: Outline three feature cards with titles, supporting copy, and an optional screenshot cue.
examples: Component library, Test dashboard, Collaboration timeline

terms.title: Social proof bar
terms.shortDescription: Logos, usage stats, or quick trust badges that calm hesitation.
terms.definition: A slim strip or cluster that shows recognizable customers, outcomes, or expert quotes without hijacking the main CTA.
terms.whenToUse: Drop near the hero or right before the primary CTA repeats.
aiPhrases: Write a social proof bar headline plus three credibility stats tied to the landing page offer.
examples: Trusted by 1,200+ GTM teams • 3.8M experiments shipped

terms.title: Testimonials
terms.shortDescription: Longer-form customer quotes paired with names, roles, and outcomes.
terms.definition: Testimonials translate proof into narrative—showing what changed, how fast, and what metric moved.
terms.whenToUse: After value props or near pricing to reinforce belief before commitment.
aiPhrases: Turn this case study into a two-sentence testimonial with a named role and quant result.
examples: “We doubled signups in 45 days once we enforced the attention ratio rules.”

terms.title: FAQ
terms.shortDescription: Answer the top objections before someone bounces to support.
terms.definition: The FAQ clusters 4-6 questions ordered by frequency so teams feel confident clicking the CTA.
terms.whenToUse: Near the bottom or beside pricing when adoption blockers surface.
aiPhrases: List the top five questions a skeptical buyer asks before trying this landing page system.
examples: “How long does setup take?” with a 90-minute reassurance

terms.title: Pricing table
terms.shortDescription: Side-by-side comparison of plans or the single offer summary.
terms.definition: Pricing tables outline cost, inclusions, and commitment so there’s no mystery before the CTA.
terms.whenToUse: Whenever the landing page is selling a specific plan, package, or service tier.
aiPhrases: Compose a single-offer pricing module with price, inclusions, and a risk reducer.
examples: Growth Plan – $2,400/mo • includes CRO lead, playbook, and build crew

terms.title: Footer CTA
terms.shortDescription: Final call-to-action for visitors who read everything.
terms.definition: A mirrored primary CTA paired with contact details or a low-friction alternate action for fence sitters.
terms.whenToUse: Always repeat the CTA at the bottom for high-intent scrollers.
aiPhrases: Write a footer CTA block with a headline, CTA button, and trust microcopy.
examples: Ready to ship cleaner pages? → Book the 20-minute teardown

buckets.title: Design system elements
buckets.description: Tokens, grids, and art direction cues that keep visual polish tied to performance.

terms.title: Layout grid
terms.shortDescription: Defines columns, gutters, and breakpoints so content breathes predictably.
terms.definition: A documented grid with column counts, gutter widths, and margin behavior that designers and engineers share.
terms.whenToUse: Before final comps or responsive builds so every section aligns across devices.
aiPhrases: Outline a 12-column grid with desktop and mobile spacing rules for this landing page.
examples: Desktop: 12 columns, 80px margins, 24px gutters. Mobile: 4 columns, 16px margins.

terms.title: Type scale
terms.shortDescription: A reusable set of heading, body, and accent sizes tied to tokens.
terms.definition: Type scales list font sizes, line heights, and usage notes so hierarchy stays intentional.
terms.whenToUse: When refining hero copy, section intros, or responsive adjustments.
aiPhrases: Propose a type scale that pairs a display headline with supporting paragraph and label styles.
examples: Display 56/64, Heading 32/40, Body 18/28, Caption 14/20.

terms.title: Color tokens
terms.shortDescription: Primary, neutral, and accent values mapped to semantic usage.
terms.definition: Each token includes hex values, contrast ratios, and situations where it can appear.
terms.whenToUse: Whenever you introduce new components or want to ensure brand colors stay accessible.
aiPhrases: List primary, neutral, and status color tokens with contrast guidance for dark UI.
examples: Primary/Emerald 500 for CTAs, Slate 900 backgrounds, Amber 400 for highlights.

terms.title: Imagery brief
terms.shortDescription: Rules for photography, illustration, and mockup treatment.
terms.definition: Outlines framing, lighting, and compositional cues so visuals feel consistent and purposeful.
terms.whenToUse: Before commissioning photos or building hero mocks.
aiPhrases: Write an imagery brief describing product mock angles, texture, and lighting for this campaign.
examples: Three-quarter dashboard mock with soft shadows and muted backgrounds to keep CTA dominant.

terms.title: Component variants
terms.shortDescription: Documented states for buttons, cards, inputs, and alerts.
terms.definition: Shows base, hover, active, and disabled treatments with spacing annotations.
terms.whenToUse: During dev handoff or when QA spots inconsistencies between screens.
aiPhrases: List button and card variants with padding, radius, and motion guidance.
examples: Primary button 14px/32px, 999ms easing, 2px border; Secondary ghost variant with 1px outline.

terms.title: State specs
terms.shortDescription: Micro-interactions, focus rings, and transitions captured in one place.
terms.definition: Details how elements respond to hover, focus, success, warning, and error events.
terms.whenToUse: When aligning design with engineering on accessibility and motion.
aiPhrases: Describe hover, focus, and loading states for CTAs and form inputs on this page.
examples: CTA hover raises 2px with glow, focus shows 2px dashed outline, loading swaps label with spinner.

buckets.title: UX flow playbook
buckets.description: Experience artifacts that keep every interaction confident and conversion-focused.

terms.title: Journey map
terms.shortDescription: Chronological view of user intent, emotions, and touchpoints.
terms.definition: Maps each stage from awareness to conversion, capturing needs, questions, and supporting assets.
terms.whenToUse: Ahead of redesigns or when stitching marketing pages to in-product onboarding.
aiPhrases: Draft a journey map table that lists stage, goal, mentality, and supporting content.
examples: Stage: Consider → Goal: prove credibility → Asset: testimonial strip.

terms.title: Micro flow
terms.shortDescription: Step-by-step outline for a single key task.
terms.definition: Breaks a task like booking a teardown into discrete screens, decisions, and expected feedback.
terms.whenToUse: When engineering needs clarity on edge cases or copy teams script tooltips.
aiPhrases: Detail the micro flow for submitting the hero brief, including alternate paths.
examples: Step 2: Upload assets → Validation: size + format → Confirmation toast.

terms.title: Friction log
terms.shortDescription: Running list of every hesitation, confusion, or stall users report.
terms.definition: Captures issue, location, severity, and hypothesis for why it happens.
terms.whenToUse: During usability tests or post-launch monitoring.
aiPhrases: Turn research notes into a friction log with impact scores and recommended fixes.
examples: Issue: CTA hidden on mobile hero → Severity: High → Fix: sticky bar.

terms.title: Progressive disclosure model
terms.shortDescription: Plan for revealing detail only when the user signals intent.
terms.definition: Specifies default, hover, and expanded states so complex info never overwhelms.
terms.whenToUse: Pricing tables, feature breakdowns, or FAQs that risk cognitive overload.
aiPhrases: Design a progressive disclosure plan for the integration section with hover reveals.
examples: Show top three integrations, reveal setup steps after click.

terms.title: Empty state
terms.shortDescription: Guided screen that appears before data exists.
terms.definition: Combines an illustration, short benefit reminder, and CTA or sample data.
terms.whenToUse: Dashboards, saved prompts, or teardown queues with new users.
aiPhrases: Write an empty state for the teardown queue that nudges users to add their first page.
examples: “No teardowns yet” + button to upload briefs + reminder of 24h turnaround.

terms.title: Error recovery pattern
terms.shortDescription: Explains what failed, why, and how to bounce back without restarting.
terms.definition: Pairs descriptive errors with inline fixes, secondary actions, or live chat links.
terms.whenToUse: Forms, uploads, auth, or payment experiences.
aiPhrases: Create tiered error messages (gentle, blocking) for the asset uploader with next steps.
examples: Upload failed: file exceeds 25MB → Offer compression tips + link to async submission.
